clue.text: Small face with a self-satisfied expression

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
mug is slang for a person's face

explanation.surface: Someone small-faced is wearing a smirk.
explanation.definitionFit: A smirking, complacent person looks pleased with themselves, which is the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Eisteddfod winner turned up looking dreary

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a word up means reading it from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the chief prize at the Welsh Eisteddfod festival goes to a poet, crowned or chaired as bard

explanation.surface: The prize-winning poet at the Welsh festival looks gloomy as he arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: An Eisteddfod is a Welsh festival of music and poetry; BARD reads upward as DRAB. 'looking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something dull, colourless and lacking cheer.

clue.text: Employer engages you and me with hesitation

parts.note: you and me together are us
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A boss takes on a couple of people who are rather hesitant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engages' looks like a container indicator, but US and ER simply sit side by side; it serves as a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: One who employs something makes use of it, so an employer in this sense is one who uses.

clue.text: Beef initially taken up and casseroled

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word Beef

parts.note: something taken up has been lifted or raised

explanation.surface: Beef is first lifted out and then slow-cooked in a casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: Braising is slow cooking in a covered pot with a little liquid, much as a casserole is cooked.

clue.text: Listen! Drug abuse may cause moodiness

indicators.note: abuse suggests misuse or mistreatment, so the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that drug abuse can make people moody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abuse' rearranges LISTEN and DRUG; 'may' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone discontented or sulky is to bring on a bad mood in them.

clue.text: A primrose I developed for a showman

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters growing into a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener's primrose is cultivated for a theatre producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges A PRIMROSE I; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical promoter or manager who stages entertainments is a classic showman.

clue.text: Golfing tournament closed with no set limits

parts.note: the Open is golf's famous championship
something that has closed has ended

explanation.surface: A golf championship has finished with nothing limiting it.
explanation.definitionFit: An unrestricted question or arrangement has no fixed boundary or conclusion.

clue.text: Mother and I had domestic help

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
'd is the contracted form of had, as in I'd

explanation.surface: A mother and her child once employed a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A household servant who cleans and tidies is a domestic helper.

clue.text: Agent who has plenty of guts

definitions.text: Agent who has plenty of guts

parts.words: Agent who has plenty of guts
parts.note: a go-between agent, playfully read as a fellow whose midriff is ample, with a big belly

explanation.surface: A brave spy or representative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' seems to mean courage, but it is meant literally: a man with a large middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between who deals on behalf of others is an intermediary agent.

clue.text: Bargained in order to get an old Jewish cloak

indicators.note: putting the letters in order means arranging them afresh

explanation.surface: Someone haggled to obtain an ancient garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges BARGAINED; 'to get an' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The gaberdine or gabardine was a long loose coat worn especially by Jews in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Mount yielding Roman copper shilling

parts.note: the as was an ancient Roman copper coin
s is the abbreviation for the old British shilling

explanation.surface: A horse obtained for a Roman coin and a shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin worth twelve pence; 'yielding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey is an animal one can ride, so it serves as a mount.

clue.text: Forks out for rented accommodation

definitions.meaning: a gardener who forks out soil turns it over with a spade-like tool, as a dog scratches up earth
lodgings, a rented room, in informal British usage

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is turning up soil with a fork; the other is informal British slang for rented lodgings.

clue.text: Agree to have only sons

definitions.meaning: to signal agreement with a dip of the head
a family with only sons has no daughters, read as ..., the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic reading: 'no D', D being the standard abbreviation for daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip of the head shows assent; and a family of sons has zero daughters, abbreviated as letters.

clue.text: Strive to be permanently in a Cambridge college

indicators.note: in places the word for permanently inside the name of the Cambridge institution

parts.note: the Perse is a long-established school in Cambridge
ever can mean always or permanently, as in for ever

explanation.surface: A student hopes to stay at a Cambridge college for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link; PERSE is the name of a school in Cambridge, which the setter calls a college, and EVER goes in after PERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep trying in spite of difficulty is to strive steadily.

clue.text: Stir in first coat for natural starter

indicators.note: in tells us the word for stir goes inside the word for the first coat

parts.note: primer is the first coat of paint applied to a surface
to stir is to move

explanation.surface: A decorator mixes the undercoat as a starting job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. The definition plays on the philosophers' idea of the original cause of all natural motion.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy and theology this is the first cause that sets the natural world in motion; generally an initiator.

clue.text: Dash about to organise milk-delivery service

definitions.meaning: to rush busily here and there
to ..., as a milkman runs his daily round

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as RUN A ROUND: organising a milkman's route.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushing to and fro is one sense; running a milk round, the milkman's delivery route, is the other.

clue.text: Praising former job for a campanologist

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a campanologist is a bell-ringer, whose work includes tolling bells

explanation.surface: Someone is speaking well of a bell-ringer's previous occupation.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, so this is the present participle of lauding.

clue.text: Double set-back for a pre-Commonwealth archbishop

indicators.note: set back suggests the word moved backwards, read in reverse

parts.note: dual means double or twofold

explanation.surface: An archbishop suffered two reverses before Cromwell's rule.
explanation.walkthrough: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I, executed in 1645 before the Commonwealth of 1649; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: William Laud held the see of Canterbury before Cromwell's republic replaced the monarchy.

clue.text: Tidying around to gain social standing

indicators.note: around suggests letters moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone cleans up around the house to earn respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges TIDYING; 'to gain' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Status worthy of respect, a stately bearing or rank, is one sense of the word.

clue.text: An honourable lady conceals sex appeal from a man

indicators.note: the lady's title conceals the other word by holding it inside

parts.note: Dame is the title of a woman honoured with a knighthood-equivalent
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the 1920s It girl

explanation.surface: A titled lady hides her allure from a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link. A descendant of the first man in Genesis is any human being.
explanation.definitionFit: A descendant of the biblical first man, so any human being or man.

clue.text: Measure used in 10 court sessions

indicators.note: used in signals that the measure is put inside the answer to the cross-referenced clue

parts.note: the answer to 10 down, a donkey
size is a measure of dimensions

explanation.surface: A measurement is used in a cross-reference to court hearings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Assizes were periodic criminal courts held around England and Wales until 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, the periodic county courts held by travelling judges in England and Wales.

clue.text: Woman embraces one who will succeed

indicators.note: a word that embraces another holds it within its arms

parts.note: her refers to a woman
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A woman hugs her successor.
explanation.definitionFit: A successor is the person next in line to inherit a title or estate.

clue.text: Final event at the Cobblers Ball

definitions.text: Final event at the Cobblers Ball

parts.words: Final event at the Cobblers Ball
parts.note: the closing number at a dance, punning on a shoemaker's foot-shaped form at a shoemakers' party

explanation.surface: The closing number at a shoemakers' dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A cobbler's last is the foot-shaped form a shoe is made on, so a cobblers' dance is a 'last dance'.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing number at a ball, and a pun on the shoemaker's foot-shaped form.

clue.text: Decline a one pound subscription

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to pay a one-pound membership fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subscription' is a link here; the pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to be in poor health, to decline in condition.

clue.text: Hooter in a yellow limousine

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A car horn in a yellow limousine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a horn in a car, which fits the limousine, but here it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls make hooting calls, so a hooter is a playful name for the bird.

clue.text: Bean curd is distributed out about Falmouth

indicators.note: about places the rearranged letters around the letter from the town
is distributed suggests the letters spread out and rearranged

parts.note: the town's name starts with F, which the setter takes as its letter

explanation.surface: Soya curd is handed out around a Cornish port.
explanation.walkthrough: TOU (OUT rearranged by 'is distributed') goes 'about' F. Falmouth is a port in Cornwall, giving its initial F.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is curd made by coagulating soya milk.

clue.text: It makes fine wine ready for drinking?

definitions.text: It makes fine wine ready for drinking?

parts.words: It makes fine wine ready for drinking?
parts.note: a substance used to clarify wine, also read as '...', which is where wine is when it is ready to drink

explanation.surface: Something that prepares good wine for serving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like an adjective but is the verb: fining clears wine of haze, and this fish-derived gelatin is a traditional fining agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelatin from fish bladders used as a fining agent to clear wine and beer.

clue.text: Crowd of spectators by the wicket

definitions.meaning: the number attending a match, or the money they pay
a wicket is a small door or ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link. 'wicket' suggests cricket, but here it means a small gate.
explanation.definitionFit: The attendance at a sports event is its turnout; a wicket is also a small barrier opening.

clue.text: Eager to have Saul's successor beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: David followed Saul as king of Israel

explanation.surface: Someone longs to see the king's heir decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have' is a link; DAVID loses his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and enthusiastic are synonyms of eager.

clue.text: Di went back in Home Counties team

indicators.note: in puts the reversed name inside the region's abbreviation

parts.note: the Home Counties lie in South East England, abbreviated SE

indicators.note: went back means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Di is taken as written, a girl's name

explanation.surface: Di returned to play in a team from the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are those surrounding London; ID (Di reversed by 'went back') goes inside SE.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a side is a team, as in the home side.

clue.text: Make one's way to the Mayfair area

definitions.meaning: Mayfair is in London's West End

explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. Mayfair is an upmarket district of the West End of London, W being the abbreviation for West.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on one's way is the verb sense; the West End of London, shortened, is the other.

clue.text: Geniuses take care in Oxford classics course

indicators.note: in puts the word for take care inside the name of the course

parts.note: Greats is the Oxford name for the classics degree, Literae Humaniores
to mind is to take care, as in mind the step

explanation.surface: Brilliant students are careful on Oxford's classics course.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant thinkers are geniuses, as in the saying about such people thinking alike.
